title: Rules-based ground and duty spotter with procedural checklist

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” audit round 1, commit 5e064ff (branch sprint-5-ground-duty-spotter),
clean tree. Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

Requirement 6, the one flagged at pre-review as most consequential and as an
automatic FAIL if breached, is met cleanly and structurally. buildProsePayload
takes AnalysisResult, not Situation, so narrative and raw facts text are not in
scope to leak, not merely omitted. It projects ground name only, label+status
only, kind+label only â€” triggeredBy and description are both dropped.
buildPrompt JSON.stringify's exactly that object and nothing else, so the object
inspected is genuinely the object transmitted. prose-payload.test.ts plants a
marker string inside triggeredBy and description and asserts it cannot reach the
payload. That is the right way to test this. No finding here.

Also confirmed: ground mapping is separate and does not import or chain
concern-fact-pattern-bridge.ts; IdentifiedGround narrows ground to
V1SpottedGround and CONCERN_TO_GROUND is typed Record<ConcernCategory, readonly
V1SpottedGround[]>, so a rule emitting "religion" fails to compile; @anthropic-ai/sdk
is imported in prose-layer.ts and nowhere else; no rules module touches network,
clock or randomness; every ground is traceable via closed-vocabulary
"concern: X" strings; no liability, likelihood, probability or percentage
language in any output string (the sole grep hit instructs the model not to
produce one); lib/types.ts changes are bounded to requirement 12. All nine
requirement-13 cases exist. Vitest 49/49 pass. tsc --noEmit clean.

REQUIRED BEFORE SHIP:

1. [HIGH] The documentation-requested item asserts a duty step was satisfied on
   evidence that does not establish it â€” lib/procedural-checklist-rules.ts:23-29,
   label at :50-51.

   The item reads "Medical or functional-abilities documentation was requested
   before any request was denied". statusFromPrompt returns "done" whenever
   facts[1] holds any non-whitespace text. facts[1] asks "What documentation or
   medical information has been exchanged?" (components/IntakeFlow.tsx:553).

   That is two unsupported inferences stacked. Exchanged does not mean
   requested, and nothing in the prompt, the response, or the rule establishes
   the temporal claim "before any request was denied" at all.

   Concrete reachable failure: the employer writes "She gave us a doctor's note
   after we'd already denied the request." Substantive text, so status is "done",
   so the checklist tells the employer this procedural step was satisfied while
   they are in the middle of describing the exact gap the tool exists to spot.

   It compounds. escalation-trigger-rules.ts:57 fires the internal-action
   trigger only when status !== "done", so the same wrong "done" also suppresses
   "Request a functional abilities form" â€” the only internal-action trigger this
   sprint produces. The tool goes quiet precisely where it should speak.

   Requirement 5 forbids asserting a duty was failed without establishment, and
   the code honours that completely â€” "not-done" is never emitted by any path.
   The symmetric assertion, that a duty was satisfied, is outside requirement 5's
   literal wording and is at least as damaging in a gap-spotting tool. Dev Team
   disclosed the design candidly in the doc comment at :12-21. Disclosure is not
   the same as safe to ship, and this is the sprint's core deliverable.

   The resolution is Master Controller's, not Dev Team's, so this is recorded as
   a required fix that blocks the gate rather than a code change to make now.
   Either documentation-requested returns "insufficient-information" until intake
   asks a question that actually establishes the answer â€” which makes the
   checklist wholly inert and guts requirement 3, see finding 5 â€” or Sprint 3
   gains a structured question and this rule reads it. Both are amendments.

2. [MEDIUM] Every prose-layer failure is swallowed â€” lib/prose-layer.ts:50.

   The bare `catch {}` discards the error object entirely. Requirement 11 asks
   for degradation and degradation works correctly. It does not ask for silence.
   A revoked key, a systematic timeout, or a malformed response is
   indistinguishable from "no key configured", permanently, with nothing
   recorded anywhere. CLAUDE.md lists error-handling conventions as not yet
   decided, so I am not prescribing a specific logger â€” but throwing the error
   away is itself a decision, and it is the one that makes an outage invisible.

3. [MEDIUM] Requirement 11's failure paths are untested, and analyzeAndPhrase has
   no test at all.

   lib/prose-layer.test.ts covers only the missing-API-key branch. The catch path
   â€” network error, timeout, malformed response â€” is never exercised.
   lib/issue-analysis.ts, where "degrades to the structured rules output rather
   than failing the request" actually happens, has no test file at all. Requirement
   13 does not list one, so this is not a requirement-13 violation. Requirement 11
   is still a stated requirement whose behaviour currently rests on untested code.
   An injected failing client, or a fetch-level stub, covers both.

4. [MEDIUM] ORDERED_GROUNDS duplicates the exported V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS â€”
   lib/ground-rules.ts:61-66.

   The comment directly above it says to iterate the order declared in
   lib/types.ts. The code then declares a private copy of that order instead of
   importing the constant that already holds it (types.ts:157-162). The local
   array is typed readonly V1SpottedGround[], which does not require
   exhaustiveness, so adding a fifth ground to V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS compiles clean
   and silently drops that ground from every result. Currently identical, so no
   wrong output today. Import the constant and iterate it.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER â€” not defects, decisions:

5. Two of the three checklist items are constants. alternatives-explored and
   analysis-documented are hardcoded "insufficient-information" because Sprint 3's
   intake never asks about either, in any structured or free-text form.
   Requirement 3 asks for the items and the items exist, and given no signal at
   all, "insufficient-information" is the correct and honest output â€” requirement
   5's caution demands exactly that. Dev Team flagged it in a code comment
   (procedural-checklist-rules.ts:35-44); elevating it here so it reaches you
   rather than living in a comment nobody outside this audit will read.

   Read together with finding 1, the position is worth stating plainly: the
   checklist cannot presently distinguish a compliant employer from a
   non-compliant one on any of its three items. Two are constant regardless of
   input, and the third is "done" for any non-empty answer. That is a
   requirements gap in what Sprint 3 collects, not sloppy work by Dev Team, and
   it needs an intake amendment to close.

STANDING LIMIT, restated because it matters more on this sprint than any other:
I verified structure, traceability, purity, type narrowing, and the absence of
legal conclusions. I did not verify that the rules are legally correct â€” that
CONCERN_TO_GROUND maps interpersonal-conflict to sex defensibly, or that these
three checklist items are the right duty-to-accommodate line items. That is law,
not code, and no gate in this workflow can check it. The sprint's own
Dependencies section says Chang should review this sprint's rules output before
Sprint 6 renders it to anyone. That review is still outstanding and this PASS
does not substitute for it.

Re-audit required. Finding 1 needs a Master Controller decision before Dev Team
can act on it. Do not run /sprint-dev-done on this verdict.
